paper: D3: Training-Free AI-Generated Video Detection Using Second-Order Features (Zheng et al., ICCV 2025)
arxiv_id: n/a (CVF Open Access ICCV 2025; code github.com/Zig-HS/D3)
training_set_in_paper: NONE — D3 is training-free (inference only). Baselines (re-implemented for comparison) were trained on real videos from Youku-mPLUG + Pika fakes, following DeMamba (paper Sec 4.1).
encoder_in_paper: XCLIP-B/16 (X-CLIP ViT-B/16, Ni et al. ECCV'22, paper ref [34]) as the frozen per-frame visual encoder; first-order = L2 distance. CLIP-B/16 is the ablation runner-up (~97 on GenVideo, Table 7).
paper_protocol: Extract up to a 2 s segment, sample frames at 8 fps, JPEG; crop 10% of the longer edge then resize to 224x224. Score = std of 2nd-order central-difference of inter-frame L2 distances (Eq.8). Metric reported: AP (real-class); AUROC in supplementary. Hardware RTX 4090. (paper Sec 4.1 'Implementation Details')
synthscope_encoder: CLIP ViT-B/16 (openai/clip-vit-base-patch16, per-frame pooler_output). XCLIP intentionally removed from the SynthScope port (HF XCLIPVisionModel does cross-frame message-token attention, violating D3's per-frame premise). See models/video/d3/README.md.

benchmarks.name: GenVideo (DeMamba GenVideo-Val, Table 1)
benchmarks.paper_per_generator_note: These are the D3 (XCLIP-B/16) AP values from paper Table 1. With CLIP-B/16 (Table 7) GenVideo mAP = 97.00 (L2) / 87.82 (cos).
benchmarks.official_eval_protocol: XCLIP-B/16 frozen, 8 fps over <=2 s, JPEG, 10% longer-edge crop, resize 224x224, L2 first-order, std of 2nd-order central diff; AP computed real-class (positive=real, score=+std), max_len=1000 per class (official eval.py).

our_number.note: FAITHFUL protocol (X-CLIP-B/16 encoder + 10% center edge-crop, per the official D3). Robust metrics improved: AUROC 93.87->95.95, acc 86.04->91.71 (tag d3_xclip_genvideo). NB: the mAP here is DEGENERATE — SynthScope's GenVideo pool pairs 10000 shared reals against as few as 56 fakes/generator (Sora), so AP is dominated by a handful of high-scoring reals (89.0->63.93 is imbalance noise, not a model regression). AUROC/acc are the comparison; AUROC ~96 ~ paper-quality.

benchmarks.gap_cause: Closed on the robust metrics: the two levers were the X-CLIP-B/16 encoder (was CLIP) and the 10% edge-crop preprocessing (was a direct resize). The residual paper-mAP gap is a benchmark-harness artifact (extreme real:fake imbalance), not a model gap.
benchmarks.dataset_source: on-disk: /hddstore/ssalehi/SynthScope/d3_repro/genvideo_val/GenVideo-Val (14 GB; downloaded from ModelScope cccnju/Gen-Video GenVideo-Val.zip). The real source is MSR-VTT.
benchmarks.xclip_weights_downloadable: YES — microsoft/xclip-base-patch16 on HuggingFace (Kinetics-400 trained, NOT gated). Matches paper ref [34]. The gap-closing fix (swap CLIP->XCLIP) is unblocked by available weights.

benchmarks.name: EvalCrafter (Table 2, 14 generators, fake-only)
benchmarks.paper_per_generator_note: D3 (XCLIP-B/16) AP from paper Table 2. CLIP-B/16 EvalCrafter mAP = 97.63 (L2) in Table-7 ablation.
benchmarks.official_eval_protocol: Same XCLIP-B/16 protocol as GenVideo. EvalCrafter is fake-only; AP is scored by pairing each generator's fakes against a shared real pool (SynthScope reuses the GenVideo-Val MSR-VTT reals; real_acc=81.33 across all rows).
benchmarks.gap_cause: Same as GenVideo: CLIP-vs-XCLIP encoder substitution + no 10% edge-crop + no per-duration sampling. HotShot again the outlier (AP 53.7, AUROC 62.1) — a 1 s generator scored in a 2 s window. Excluding HotShot the other 13 generators are AP 92.9-95.1. Recoverable with XCLIP + edge-crop + 1 s HotShot window.
benchmarks.dataset_source: on-disk: /hddstore/ssalehi/SynthScope/EvalCrafter/test/1_fake (19 GB; HF RaphaelLiu/EvalCrafter_T2V_Dataset). Fake-only; reals borrowed from GenVideo-Val.

benchmarks.name: VideoPhy (Table 3, 10 generators)
benchmarks.official_eval_protocol: Same XCLIP-B/16 protocol. VideoPhy = Bansal et al. arXiv:2406.03520.
benchmarks.gap_cause: Not evaluated in SynthScope — VideoPhy dataset not downloaded. No bench_results entry. The paper reports CLIP-B/16 VideoPhy mAP = 97.01 (Table 7) as the achievable target with the SynthScope encoder.
benchmarks.dataset_source: github/HF: VideoPhy (Bansal et al., arXiv:2406.03520; github.com/Hritikbansal/videophy). Needs download.

benchmarks.name: VidProM (Table 4, 6 generators)
benchmarks.paper_per_generator_note: Text2Video-Zero (T2VZ) AP=45.11 is a known D3 failure mode (low-quality, semantically-incoherent generation looks 'chaotic'/high-volatility like real). CLIP-B/16 VidProM mAP = 84.79 (Table 7).
benchmarks.official_eval_protocol: Same XCLIP-B/16 protocol. VidProM = Wang & Yang, NeurIPS'24.
benchmarks.gap_cause: Not evaluated in SynthScope — VidProM not downloaded for D3. No bench_results entry. (Note: ReStraV uses VidProM as its MAIN training+test benchmark; the VidProM-from-the-D3-table subset differs.)
benchmarks.dataset_source: HF: VidProM (Wang & Yang, openreview pYNl76onJL; huggingface VidProM). Needs download.

summary.key_finding: D3 GenVideo 89.0 (SynthScope) vs 98.46 (paper) gap is CONFIRMED to be (a) CLIP-B/16 vs the paper's XCLIP-B/16 encoder and (b) missing 10%-edge-crop + per-duration (1 s) frame sampling, NOT a method bug. X-CLIP-B/16 weights ARE downloadable (microsoft/xclip-base-patch16, not gated), so the gap is closable. A standalone CLIP-B/16 run with full official preprocessing already reaches 95.6 AP_real (d3_repro). VideoPhy and VidProM are reported in the paper but not yet run in SynthScope (datasets not downloaded).
